summary: self-certificates ships remote-code dropper disguised as PEM key
details: The package presents itself as a self-signed-certificate helper but ships test/key.pem which masquerades as an RSA private key. Its body is base64 that decodes to a fake CERTIFICATE, whose body base64-decodes again into JavaScript that fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response to python3 - via spawn('python3', ['-']) with p.stdin.write(log). The inner URL is itself base64-encoded to further conceal the destination. index.js reads this file, strips the PEM armor, base64-decodes it, and passes the resulting payload to selfsign.generate(...) via the advertised generateCertificates() API, so any caller of the documented API triggers fetch-and-execute of attacker-controlled code from aptupdate.org on the host running the code. The multi-layer PEM camouflage and runtime URL reconstruction indicate deliberate evasion of static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
